parts:
Hi Fabricio,

On Sat, Mar 5, 2016 at 11:21 PM, Fabricio Mendes Fialho <fabrici...@ucla.edu> wrote:
Prof. Chambers,

I use mirt to fit IRT models and have been facing one issue regarding the extraction of information from mirt object. Listwise deletion of cases containing missing values causes a loss of approx. ~15% of cases. One way I thought to somehow address the issue is to estimate M "complete" datasets outside mirt (using mice or amelia), fit the same model using each M(i) dataset, then calculate the mean for the model parameters. A gross approach to it, but so far so good. However, I'd like to include ICC plots in my report. itemplot() can generate beautiful plots for the M(i) using its respective mirt() output object.

You really don't need to be imputing data unless the missing-mechanism is not at random. IRT models are fit using full information methods, so doing things like list-wise deletion is not required.
 

My question ends up being: What exactly does itemplot() do? I would like to extract information from each mirt output (e.g. SE, theta, P(theta) etc.), average them, and then plot the average value across the M "complete" datasets. I just cannot figure out how to do it. A similar question would come out if I just wanted, for instance, to plot ICC curves using ggplot rather than lattice.

If you must go down this route, most of the internals are available (probtrace(), testinfo(), inteminfo(), and so on). All these functions do is plot the expected tracelines/information given some Theta input, so if you want customized graphics just build them up from the smaller components.

Phil
 

If this is a recurrent question and you think it would be good to share it online, please feel free to edit it the way it pleases you.

I apologize for the inconvenience.

Sincerely,
Fabricio
